patient._comment: 'patient' contains the three sections that may be exposed in the detailed patient display: presentation, answer, and clinical.

presentation._comment: The immutable patient evidence package available for triage. Panel context controls whether other sections are locked or available.
presentation.chiefComplaint: Fell from the top of the pyramid
presentation.quote: I was literally mid 'Go Boston U' and the base wobbled. I landed on my head and shoulders. Everything moves fine, it just really hurts right here in my neck.
presentation.triageNote: 21-year-old female who fell about ten feet from a cheerleading stunt onto her head and shoulders, with midline cervical tenderness, GCS 15 and no neurological deficit.

answer._comment: The authoritative game answer. Explicit ESI, destination, and destination rationale are answer-bearing content; the player's assignment remains session state.
answer.destinationReason: ESI 3 is appropriate because this stable dangerous-mechanism neck injury is expected to require multiple trauma-assessment and imaging resources.

clinical._comment: Display-ready clinical interpretation derived from patient.presentation. It preserves clinical meaning but must not explicitly name or identify the correct ESI level or destination; it does not participate in scoring.
clinical.summary: This alert patient has midline cervical tenderness after a ten-foot axial-load fall onto the head and shoulders.
clinical.acuityReason: Normal neurologic findings are reassuring, but the mechanism and midline tenderness require immobilization and imaging before clearance.
expectedResources: Trauma examination and additional imaging as indicated
teachingPoints: A normal neurologic examination does not exclude an unstable cervical injury.
Spinal motion restriction should be maintained until appropriate clinical and imaging clearance.

possibleClinicalOutcome.disposition: Trauma evaluation and imaging would guide discharge in a collar, specialist consultation, or admission if structural injury is found.

aiImageGeneration._comment: 'aiImageGeneration' is info for AI to generate the image of the patient. Most images were done with openAI gpt-image-1 using an API, not the app, in July 2026. Look for some python scripts that are used to create these images. Be sure that the anchor-image is available and is provided to the AI - otherwise the images will not be consistent.
aiImageGeneration.who: a 21-year-old black woman, a university senior, in a scarlet-and-white cheerleading uniform with 'BU' on the front, seated upright on a blue padded clinic chair
aiImageGeneration.pose: sitting very upright and still, holding her own neck with one hand, afraid to turn her head
aiImageGeneration.expression: tense and carefully controlled, trying not to move
signs: one hand supporting the back of her own neck
aiImageGeneration.lookSeverity: alert and stable, holding herself deliberately still
aiImageGeneration.prompt: Softly-shaded painterly cartoon illustration in a semi-realistic Pixar/Disney style: smooth gradient shading, soft natural lighting, gentle rounded volumes, fine delicate outlines (NOT thick flat cartoon outlines), warm detailed rendering, natural realistic proportions, single character. Match the painterly STYLE of the attached reference image - its brushwork, shading, line weight, lighting and palette - but do NOT copy its cropping, camera distance or composition. FRAMING (follow exactly): a full-body WIDE SHOT, square 1:1, 3/4 front view, subject centred. The ENTIRE figure must be inside the frame from the top of the head to the soles of both feet, and the ENTIRE chair must be inside the frame including all four chair legs meeting the floor. Leave clear empty margin on all four sides - roughly 10% of the image width as space above the head and below the feet. This is NOT a close-up, NOT a bust, NOT a head-and-shoulders portrait, NOT a cropped view: the camera is pulled well back so the whole person and the whole chair sit comfortably inside the picture with room around them. Draw the COMPLETE body - head, neck, torso, both arms, both hands, lap, both legs, both feet with shoes. Nothing cropped by the edges, no missing or truncated limbs, no body part fading out or left unfinished. ANATOMY AND OBJECTS (critical): exactly one head, exactly two arms ending in exactly two hands, exactly two legs ending in two feet, five fingers on each hand. No extra, duplicated, floating or partial limbs. All furniture is solid and fully opaque - the chair must never look transparent, and its back, seat and legs must all be completely drawn. Subject: a 21-year-old black woman - a fully grown ADULT WOMAN in her early twenties, a university senior. Draw adult facial structure: defined cheekbones, a defined adult jawline, adult proportions with a head that is proportionally smaller relative to her body than a child's, and the height and build of a grown woman athlete. She is emphatically NOT a child and NOT a high-school teenager - she should read instantly as a woman in her twenties. She wears a scarlet-and-white cheerleading uniform with two bold white block letters 'BU' across the front of the top, and is seated upright on a blue padded clinic chair. Pose: sitting very upright and rigidly still, one hand supporting the back of her own neck, plainly afraid to turn her head. Expression: tense and carefully controlled, trying hard not to move. Clearly visible: one hand supporting the back of her own neck; the head held rigidly straight; the letters 'BU' across the front of a scarlet-and-white cheer uniform; a young adult woman in her twenties. Overall: alert and stable, holding herself deliberately still. The ONLY text anywhere in the picture is the two letters 'BU' - no other lettering, no watermarks, no border.
